routing_warnings.description: The reported reversal concerns which site content was placed on each Wix profile rather than the master site's location-selection routing behavior.
The unlinked location button concerns master-site routing to a location website, not future-location extensibility.
This repeats the missing location-button link and belongs to location discovery and routing.
The message reports that master-site and Ridgehaven content were assigned to the wrong sites or profiles.
The question about using the same domain concerns public domain attachment, which is separate from profile ownership.
The alternative instruction to attach each domain to the correct account also affects the domain-to-website mapping Requirement.
This message states that the domain can be attached to the correct website and does not claim that site profiles were corrected.
The client verifies only that the domain connects to the correct website; this does not verify account-bound content, settings, or profile mapping.
The reported reversal concerns which site content was placed on each Wix profile rather than public domain attachment.
The client explicitly requests that each website be associated with the correct profile.
The concern about account-bound settings and subscriptions concerns profile/account ownership beyond domain routing.
The client reports that the Ridgehaven and Shatter House USA site profiles were placed on the wrong websites; this concerns site content-to-profile mapping rather than brand identity.
The location-selection menu and routing clause belongs to the master-site location discovery and routing Requirement; only the activity-listing clause applies to the target Requirement.
The separate observation that the website lacks booking software concerns location booking behavior rather than package and pricing consistency.
The clause making the Ridgehaven page a template for future locations belongs to the future-location expansion Requirement rather than the temporary coming-soon page lifecycle.
The client reports incorrect branding in the mockup and requires the Shatter House logo; this concerns brand identity rather than the coming-soon page state.
The unlinked button refers through message 142 to the master site's coming-soon location link, not to the Ridgehaven page's own opening-state controls.
The booking-system installation claim concerns location booking setup rather than implementation of the coming-soon page.
The reported failure concerns Ridgehaven and Shatter House USA content being assigned to the wrong sites, not the internal behavior of the Ridgehaven coming-soon page.
The reported reversal of the Ridgehaven and Shatter House USA site profiles concerns correct content-to-profile mapping rather than reuse of legacy source material.
The request to copy the site into the other profile is a proposed correction to the reversed profile assignment, not a change to the legacy-content reuse requirement.

In the context of message 13, the client's acceptance confirms that the Harbor Valley site should remain live during the transition; this is a transition-availability decision rather than an SEO-preservation change.
The client reports that the preview uses incorrect branding and requires the Shatter House logo; this is a brand-identity failure rather than a failure to supply the mockup.
The client specifies correct imagery for axe throwing and splatter-room activities.
The client changes or clarifies the visual reference expected for the website design.
The client explicitly confirms that the competitor website, rather than the mockup, is the design reference.
The unlinked location button concerns routing from the master site, not whether separate location websites exist.
The complaint that the two websites look identical concerns their content differentiation rather than the separate-website architecture.
The requested location-selection menu and links concern master-site location discovery and routing.
The reversed Ridgehaven and Shatter House USA content belongs to the site content-to-profile mapping Requirement.
The missing-packages clause concerns consistent package content; the booking-software clause cannot be retained here because the affected website is not resolved by the exchange.
The client reports missing booking software, not a calendar-isolation failure.
The freelancer claims installation of the booking system on the second website but does not specifically claim calendar isolation.
The stated limitation concerns separate payout accounts under a single Wix payment account and primarily supports the payout-isolation lifecycle.
The implementation claim concerns installation of the booking system, not location-specific payment processing.
